common_name: Clematis 'Patricia Ann Fretwell' (double pink large-flowered clematis)

planting.note: Plant with the crown 2-3 inches below soil level to encourage resilient new growth from below ground, and provide a trellis or obelisk for its compact climbing habit.

directions: This early large-flowered cultivar opens fully double, soft pink blooms with a deeper pink central bar in late spring, then follows with single or semi-double flowers of the same soft pink tone in late summer into autumn. It belongs to pruning group 2, so only light shaping and removal of dead wood is needed in late winter to preserve the spring double flush. Grow in fertile, well-drained soil with the roots shaded and the top in sun, and water regularly during establishment and dry spells.

planting.note: Site with roots in cool, shaded soil and the vine climbing into sun on a trellis, fence, or through a shrub.

directions: A vigorous Dutch introduction (raised by K. Maarse Dzn Jr.) prized for its enormous vivid rosy-purple flowers with darker veined central bars, crinkled tepal margins, and prominent red anthers, blooming from June through September. It tolerates part shade better than many large-flowered hybrids. Treat as pruning group 2, giving only light shaping and removing dead or weak wood in late winter, and mulch well to keep roots cool and moist.

common_name: Clematis 'Snow Queen' (white and mauve large-flowered clematis)

planting.note: Provide a sturdy support for climbing and keep the root zone shaded and cool while the vine reaches for sun.

directions: This classic large-flowered hybrid produces broad, slightly rippled white tepals washed with pale mauve shading at first and fading to white, set off by a central boss of stamens tipped in deep burgundy-pink, opening up to 7 inches across in late spring with a repeat flush in early fall. It falls in pruning group 2, so prune lightly in late winter and again right after the first bloom fades to encourage the second flush. Grow in fertile, moist, well-drained soil in full sun to part shade for the best flower color and vigor.

planting.note: No trellis needed; grow in a container or front-of-border spot where its low mounding habit can be appreciated.

directions: A dwarf Guernsey-bred (Raymond Evison) selection that forms a dense, flower-covered mound only about a foot tall with no need for a trellis, making it well suited to containers, hanging baskets, and small-garden borders. It bears abundant violet-mauve flowers with pointed, ruffled, star-shaped petals from late spring into midsummer. Grow in well-drained, consistently moist, nutrient-rich soil in full to partial sun, and deadhead spent blooms to encourage continued flowering.

planting.note: Train onto an obelisk, low trellis, or large container; needs no hard pruning since it flowers on old wood.

directions: A distinctive Korean-species selection noted for nodding, double, bell-shaped flowers in an unusual amber to creamy-yellow shade, shaded with soft pink on the reverse of the ribbed tepals, blooming in late spring with a lighter second flush in early fall followed by attractive seedheads. It is pruning group 1, flowering on old wood, so only tidy up after bloom rather than cutting hard back. Grow in moist, well-drained soil in full sun to light shade, and keep the root zone cool with mulch.

planting.note: Give a trellis, arbor, or obelisk to climb and keep roots cool and shaded for best bloom.

directions: This early large-flowered selection opens icy violet-blue blooms with contrasting dark red stamens, rounded in the first spring flush and becoming more star-shaped in later waves of bloom through late summer. Because it flowers on both old and new growth, only light pruning of dead or weak stems is needed in late winter to keep a tidy framework. Plant in fertile, neutral to slightly alkaline, well-drained soil in full to part sun for the longest repeat bloom.

common_name: Clematis florida 'Fond Memories' (outlined white large-flowered clematis)

planting.note: Best in a sheltered spot against a warm wall or trellis; in colder zones, grow in a large container that can be moved to protection in winter.

directions: A vigorous Clematis florida selection bearing large single flowers of six white petals edged with a fine magenta outline around purple anthers, earning it a place among the 'outlined white' clematis, blooming from June through October. Clematis florida types generally appreciate a sheltered, warm position, so give winter protection to the crown in the colder end of its range. Prune lightly as a group 2 plant, removing only dead or weak growth, and grow in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun.

planting.note: No support needed; let it weave through low perennials or spill from a container as a mounding groundcover.

directions: Part of a dwarf patio clematis series, this low, spreading selection forms a mounding groundcover only about a foot tall and up to 4 feet wide, bearing single to semi-double, pale silvery-blue flowers with softly ruffled edges and red-brown anthers from late spring into summer. Its sprawling habit makes it useful for weaving among taller perennials or spilling over container edges. Grow in well-drained soil in full sun to part shade, and trim lightly after the main flush to tidy the mound.
sources: North Carolina State Extension plant toolbox

common_name: Clematis 'Chantilly' (pale pink fading to white compact clematis)

planting.note: Compact habit suits a small trellis, obelisk, or large container; shade the roots while allowing the vine to climb into sun.

directions: A compact, slightly fragrant selection bearing mostly single flowers that open pale pink with a darker central bar and age toward white, set off by dark red anthers on white filaments, blooming in two flushes from late spring to early summer and again in late summer into fall. Its naturally small stature suits containers and tight spaces better than many large-flowered climbers. As a group 2 bloomer, prune lightly in late winter, and grow in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun.

planting.note: Train over a hoop, obelisk, or low fence; its long, near-evergreen growing season benefits from a sheltered site in colder parts of its range.

directions: A Guernsey-raised (Evison/Poulsen) selection bearing fully double flowers in a rich plum-red that form a rosette shape, flowering over an unusually long season from early summer to early autumn with near-evergreen foliage in milder climates. Its long flowering stems make it well suited to training around hoops or low supports rather than tall structures. Prune as a group 3 plant, cutting back hard in late winter, and grow in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun with the roots shaded.
